reason: ArenaTableCell draws a cell box -- the padding, the alignment and the mono/gold treatment its column asks for, or in card mode a label/value pair or a full-width block -- and projects whatever the consumer put in it. It manages no state, and with no `href` it owns no interactive element either: any ArenaBadge, ArenaButton or link inside comes from `children`, caller-supplied content, not from ArenaTableCell itself. With `href` it draws one interactive element of its own, a real <a href>, and the binding still holds: there is no link pattern to bind, and that is not an omission, because a link's role, its keyboard activation and its focusability all arrive the moment the element is an anchor -- the same reading ArenaSideNavItem records for its own `link` case. What the cell adds on top of the anchor is the settled activation split, which is a convention rather than a clause of any pattern. What it DOES carry is not its own affordance either: the cell role comes from the <td> it is, and the roving `tabIndex` and the focus ring belong to the enclosing ArenaTable's `grid` binding and are injected by it, which is why they are absent from this contract's members as well as from this pattern. In card mode it declares role="presentation", which is not an affordance either but the removal of one: below the breakpoint the box is a label beside a value and not a cell of anything.
